questions.stem: If g(x) = 4f(x), how is the graph of f transformed to obtain g?

options.A: Horizontally stretched by a factor of 4
options.B: Vertically stretched by a factor of 4
options.D: Reflected across the y-axis

questions.explanation: B is correct. Multiplying the output scales all y-values by the factor.

questions.stem: If g(x) = f(x + 4), how is the graph of f transformed to obtain g?

options.A: Shifted right 4 units
options.B: Shifted up 4 units
options.D: Vertically stretched by a factor of 4

questions.explanation: C is correct. Adding h inside the input shifts the graph left by h.

questions.stem: If g(x) = f(x - 5) + 6, how is the graph of f transformed to obtain g?

options.A: Shifted left 5 units and up 6 units
options.B: Shifted right 5 units and down 6 units
options.D: Shifted right 5 units and up 6 units

questions.explanation: D is correct. Replacing x by x-h shifts right, and adding k shifts up.

questions.stem: If g(x) = -f(x) + 6, how is the graph of f transformed to obtain g?

options.A: Reflected across the x-axis and shifted up 6 units
options.B: Reflected across the y-axis and shifted up 6 units
options.C: Shifted down 6 units without a reflection
options.D: Vertically stretched by a factor of 6

questions.explanation: A is correct. Multiplying every output by -1 reflects the graph across the x-axis, and adding the constant shifts it upward.
